newsitem.title: AFGHANISTAN: Western aid groups to talk to new Afghan rulers.
newsitem.headline: Western aid groups to talk to new Afghan rulers.

text.p: Western aid agencies drafted an appeal to Kabul's new hardline Islamist rulers on Saturday to allow women workers to return to their aid jobs helping needy Afghans, United Nations coordinator Terry Pitzner said.
Western aid efforts in war-battered Afghanistan are heavily dependent on Afghan women and have been hard hit by a Taleban ban on women working.
Pitzner told reporters that the neutrally-worded appeal was likely to be delivered to the Taleban ruling council on Monday.
He said it stressed "the need for 100 percent of our workforce to implement our programmes, that without our full staff we are incapacitated in delivering humanitarian assistance."

Many Afghan women work for aid agencies delivering aid to some 200,000 people a day in Kabul, a city with an estimated population of 1.2 million, and across Afghanistan where war has been the norm for much of the past 17 years.
Aid groups say that because of the Taleban ban on women working most of their projects have ground to a halt since Taleban militia captured Kabul in a lightning strike on September 27.
Some aid officials say Kabul's new rulers have offered a sympathetic ear to western aid groups' concerns about women.

But others say that unless there is a firm and public change in the Taleban attitude, western aid is at risk because most groups have a mandate that forbids gender discrimination. Western donor governments might simply refuse to provide more money for further aid.

The groups are due to launch their annual appeal for aid to Afghanistan in early December and aid officials said the Taleban needed to show public flexibility before then if funding was to continue to flow.
